newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up in very active trading on Thursday with the lively domestic A share markets sucking liquidity out of the repo market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 14.31 percent from 12.50 percent on Wednesday.
Turnover rose to 16.09 million lots from 6.56 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Both Shanghai and Shenzhen A share marekts surged today on a continuation of the bull-run which began in April this year.
Another factor for the repo rate rises was the issue in Shanghai today of A shares in Eastern Communications Co, a key telecommunications equipment firm, traders said.
Traders believe the strong trend on the A share markets will continue to support the rates in the short term.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended down on very weak market sentiment, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 120.60 yuan from 121.60 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market increased to 1.55 million lots from 1.05 million.
